title: Pure Substances and Mixtures
summary: 'Pure' milk isn't pure to a scientist! Learn what makes a substance pure, and the two kinds of mixture.

ib.note: Foundation for elements, compounds and mixtures in MYP 3

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 8: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
Ch 2: Is Matter Around Us Pure?, section 2.1

objectives: I can explain the scientific meaning of a pure substance.
I can tell the difference between a pure substance and a mixture using the particle model.
I can classify mixtures as homogeneous (uniform) or heterogeneous (non-uniform).
I can use melting and boiling points to test whether a substance is pure.
misconceptions: 'Pure' on a label (pure ghee, pure honey) means chemically pure.
If something looks the same everywhere, it must be pure.
